correctness.rationale: All n>=3, all positive prices: first-step expectations give exact worst omitted-edge identity. An arbitrary simplex mixture and Cauchy yield universal lower bound. Strict concavity and KKT give unique threshold and positive dual weights, with at least two active coordinates. The normalized clipped rates attain the lower bound via the threshold identity, and Cauchy equality enforces unique rate vector. Boundary price equalities are covered explicitly. 385 rational dual systems, 100 exact absorbing-generator systems and 1815 normalized random feasible comparisons provide finite supplementary corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Explicit clipped price-threshold classification for the worst of all directed continuous-time pair hitting times, including exact unique optimizer and all-price threshold law, is not implied by the inspected published average-hitting, stationary-distribution-bound, cyclic-dwell, or fixed-graph results. Closest mathematical challenge is Breen--Kirkland (2017) on maximum discrete-time first-passage; its graph/stationary bound does not optimize physical holding rates against arbitrary linear prices. A specialized historical precedent remains possible.
residual_risks: A specialized earlier result for costed Markov renewal cycles or optimally weighted directed cycles may be unpublished or absent from indexed searches.
Only a same-model proof and literature assessment were conducted; independent scientific validation is not represented.
The target is distinct from first-return and stationary-weighted hitting objectives; literature using those words differently may conceal equivalent results.

value.rationale: Natural exact minimax latency allocation for irreversible cyclic transitions under a physical linear rate-resource budget. For arbitrary n and real prices, identifies all rates and optimum, unique optimizer, cheap-edge equalization and expensive-edge square-root scaling, uniform-price threshold and O(n log n) computational rule. In three-state example c=(1,3,100), improves minimax latency 208 to 144; structural transition gives information generic convexity methods do not alone provide.
